cases.prompt: Create a report focused on model design and feature engineering.
expected: Model and feature sections receive prominence.
No operations or governance section appears without relevant evidence.

cases.prompt: Create a report on evaluation correctness and current performance.
expected: Evaluation architecture leads.
Model implementation detail is compressed.

cases.prompt: Compare iterations=1 with iterations=3 on the same evidence.
expected: One-shot has one planned composition.
Three iterations contain two critique and targeted-revision cycles, not blind regeneration.

cases.prompt: Render a fixture with a material visual defect.
expected: Visual QA records a named defect.
A later render verifies the repair before passing.

cases.prompt: Compose from evidence that maps one finding to several possible taxonomies.
expected: One canonical explanation exists.
Actions may refer to it without full repetition.
Preflight or visual review flags the defects.
Layout is revised and the final render is rechecked.

cases.prompt: Add material evidence after the first draft.
expected: State and plan revisions increment.
Only impacted sections are recomposed; no Additional Findings dump appears.

cases.prompt: Create a technical report focused on features when importance and ablation artifacts exist.
expected: Available feature evidence is inspected and interpreted, with attribution limits stated.
The report does not replace existing evidence with a generic recommendation to generate importance.

cases.prompt: Analyze model design when candidate comparisons, routing shares, and runtimes exist.
expected: Models are compared on behavior, incremental value, stability, and cost rather than merely listed.
Architecture justification remains conditional on evaluation validity.

cases.prompt: Analyze evaluation when per-fold, per-origin, cohort, and baseline results exist.
expected: At least one high-information stability or variation analysis is surfaced.
Aggregate metrics are contextualized rather than treated as sufficient.

cases.prompt: Create the same technical analysis at 6-8 pages and 12-16 pages.
expected: Both versions inspect the same relevant evidence surfaces.
The shorter version compresses presentation without reducing analytical depth.

cases.prompt: Create a normal technical research report with supported future opportunities and low-effort checks.
expected: A compact Research & Improvement Map remains in the report.
Supported low-hanging fruit is distinct from larger research initiatives.

cases.prompt: Create a standard report on model design, features, evaluation, and current issues.
expected: Material components explain mechanism, applicability, failure modes, empirical support status, and implication where relevant.
Inventory tables are followed by compact analytical interpretation rather than filler prose.

cases.prompt: Describe a plausible feature family for which no ablation exists.
expected: Implementation fact, technical rationale, and project-specific empirical support remain distinct.
The report states that incremental contribution is unvalidated.

cases.prompt: Run iteration two on a report whose feature section is a detailed inventory table.
expected: The review checks every semantic depth dimension rather than passing on table presence or word count.
A targeted revision adds missing interpretation and records the affected section.

cases.prompt: Render a complete report while preserving a shorter Markdown file.
expected: Markdown/PDF semantic mismatch is detected.
Completion is blocked until the persisted Markdown contains the report's semantic content.

cases.prompt: Render a six-page report with two pages containing only a few lines but broad bounding boxes.
expected: Text-density checks identify underused pages even when geometry spans the page.
The target page count does not pass until useful analysis is integrated or the report is shortened.

invariants: reviewed report plan precedes long-form composition
stable technical-report skeleton with evidence-adaptive subsections
compact executive summary for substantial reports
one canonical explanation per material finding
no empty framework sections or discovery chronology
mandatory content-depth review in iteration two; revision only for material gaps
semantic depth review always covers core reasoning and applies conditions or failure analysis only when relevant
verified fact, technical rationale, and project evidence remain distinct
significant inspected evidence mapped into report sections
page target changes composition, not investigation depth
Research & Improvement Map retained when opportunities exist
visual defects cause repair and verification
editable semantic source matches the rendered PDF
page density combines geometry and extracted information volume
